mainTopic: Remedies for a זבה and for ירקון, and whether a ירקון drink that causes sterility violates the איסור of סירוס
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's long list of folk remedies, which grows out of the משנה allowing a כוס של עיקרין on שבת to cure ירקון. First the גמרא finishes its cures for a זבה, a woman with an abnormal flow of blood. Each cure is linked by וְאִי לָא ('and if not, try the next one'), and she is often told קוּם מִזּוֹבִיךְ ('Stop your flow!'). Then the גמרא turns to ירקון: two ingredients drunk in beer cure it but cause sterility, and a second chain of backup cures follows. Along the way come a tip from רבי יוחנן, the story of רב כהנא healing רב אחא בר יוסף, and a story about a טייעא cured by leeks and heavy sweating. Then the גמרא asks whether the sterility-causing drink is even allowed, since רבי חנינא learns from 'ובארצכם לא תעשו' that סירוס of a person is forbidden. A first answer, that the sterility happens on its own, is backed by רבי יוחנן's rooster case, but רב אשי knocks out that proof. So the גמרא answers instead that the drink is for a סריס. At the end of the amud, a new challenge from רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Persian onions boiled in wine
steps.stepSummary: The list of cures for a זבה continues. Cook Persian onions in wine, give it to her to drink, and tell her to stop her flow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Containers full of Persian onions should be boiled in wine and given to her to drink, and we say to her: 'Stop your flow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a list of cures for a זבה. This line gives one cure: a wine drink made with Persian onions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence began earlier, on the previous amud. This passage picks it up mid-sentence. The formula קוּם מִזּוֹבִיךְ is spoken to the woman with almost every cure, and it will repeat all through the list.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman with an abnormal flow of blood

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a halachic ruling telling us to use these cures today. The גמרא is recording the medical practices of its time. The topic belongs here because the משנה allows certain healing drinks on שבת.

phrases.english: containers of Persian onions,
phrases.notes: Continues a sentence that began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: and boil them in wine, and give it to her to drink,
and say to her: Stop your flow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the זבה remedy list earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Persian onions boiled in wine are a cure for a זבה.

steps.title: Seating her at a crossroads and startling her
steps.stepSummary: If the first cure fails, seat her at a crossroads holding a cup of wine. Someone startles her from behind and says 'Stop your flow!'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, seat her at a crossroads with a cup of wine in her hand. Let someone come from behind and frighten her, and say to her: 'Stop your flow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next cure in the chain. This one works by giving her a sudden fright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words וְאִי לָא ('and if not') are the hinge of the whole list. Each new cure is offered only if the one before it did not work. This cure does not use a drink at all; it relies on a sudden scare.

keyTerms.meaning: And if not (if the previous cure didn't work)

phrases.english: And if not, seat her at a crossroads,
and let her hold a cup of wine in her hand,
and let a person come from behind her and frighten her,
and say to her: Stop your flow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next cure if step 1 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sudden fright at a crossroads is a cure for a זבה.

steps.title: Cumin, saffron and fenugreek in wine
steps.stepSummary: The next cure is a fistful each of cumin, saffron and fenugreek, cooked in wine and given to her to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, bring a fistful of cumin, a fistful of saffron, and a fistful of fenugreek. Boil them in wine, give it to her to drink, and say to her: 'Stop your flow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another drink-based cure, this time made with three spices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as in step 1: cook in wine, give it to her to drink, and speak the formula. Only the ingredients change.

phrases.english: And if not, bring a fistful of cumin
and a fistful of saffron and a fistful of fenugreek,
and boil them in wine, and give it to her to drink,
and say to her: Stop your flow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next cure if step 2 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wine drink of cumin, saffron and fenugreek is a cure for a זבה.

steps.title: Spreading on barrel seals and boiled grass
steps.stepSummary: Two more cures are applied to her body instead of drunk: sixty barrel seals, and a grass called פשיטנא boiled in wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, bring sixty barrel seals, spread them on her, and say to her: 'Stop your flow!' And if not, bring פשיטנא, boil it in wine, spread it on her, and say to her: 'Stop your flow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from cures she drinks to cures that are spread on her body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verb changes from וְנַשְׁקְיַיהּ ('give her to drink') to וְלַשְׁפְּיַהּ ('spread it on her'). That one word tells you how the cure is used. Some explain that the seals are soaked first.

keyTerms.meaning: Barrel seals (the clay stoppers of barrels)

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי שִׁיתִּין שִׁיעֵי דְּדַנָּא,
phrases.english: And if not, bring sixty barrel seals,
and spread it on her, and say to her: Stop your flow!
And if not, bring pashtina grass,
and boil it in wine, and spread it on her,
and say to her: Stop your flow!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי שִׁיתִּין שִׁיעֵי דְּדַנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next two cures if step 3 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Barrel seals, or פשיטנא boiled in wine, spread on the body are cures for a זבה.

steps.title: Burnt thistle ashes in seasonal rags
steps.stepSummary: Burn a thistle that grows on Roman thorns and place its ashes in linen rags in summer or cotton rags in winter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, bring a thistle that grows on Roman thorns and burn it. Place its ashes in linen rags in the summer and in cotton rags in the winter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a cure that uses ashes wrapped in cloth. The type of cloth depends on the season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The season detail is practical: linen is cooler for summer, and cotton (or soft wool) is warmer for winter. This exact cloth formula will come back with the ostrich egg cure in step 7.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי חַרְנוּגָא דְּהִיגְתָּא רוֹמִיתָא,
phrases.english: And if not, bring a thistle from Roman thorns,
and burn it, and place it (its ashes)
in linen rags in the summer
and in cotton rags in the winter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי חַרְנוּגָא דְּהִיגְתָּא רוֹמִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next cure if step 4 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thistle ashes in seasonal rags are a cure for a זבה.

steps.title: Moving her between seven pits
steps.stepSummary: Dig seven pits and burn young vine shoots of ערלה in them. With a cup of wine in her hand, she is moved from pit to pit, and at each one she is told to stop her flow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, dig seven pits and burn young shoots of ערלה vines in them. Put a cup of wine in her hand. Raise her from this pit and seat her in that one, and again raise her from this one and seat her in that one. At each one, say to her: 'Stop your flow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes a longer cure. She is moved from one heated pit to the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated phrase וְלוֹקְמַהּ מֵהָא וְלוֹתְבַהּ אַהָא shows the moving back and forth. The formula is said at every move (אַכֹּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא), not only once. The word יַלְדָּה in parentheses is a variant or explanatory reading for the young shoots.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit or vine of a tree in its first three years

phrases.english: And if not, dig seven pits,
and burn in them young shoots of orla vines,
and let her hold a cup of wine in her hand,
and raise her from this one and seat her on that one,
and raise her from this one and seat her on that one,
phrases.notes: The גמרא itself repeats this phrase to show the repeated moving.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַכֹּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא לֵימָא לַהּ: קוּם מִזּוֹבִיךְ.
phrases.english: and at each and every one say to her: Stop your flow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next cure if step 5 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moving her between seven pits heated with ערלה shoots is a cure for a זבה.

steps.title: Fine flour and ostrich egg ashes
steps.stepSummary: Two more cures: fine flour placed on the lower half of her body, and the ashes of a burnt ostrich egg in seasonal rags.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, bring fine flour and place it on the lower half of her body, and say to her: 'Stop your flow!' And if not, bring an ostrich egg and burn it. Place its ashes in linen rags in the summer and in cotton rags in the winter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists two more cures in a row, each starting with 'and if not.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ostrich egg cure reuses the same seasonal-rags wording as the thistle in step 5. Only the burnt material is different.

phrases.english: And if not, bring fine flour,
and place it on her from the middle downward,
and say to her: Stop your flow!

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי בֵּיעֲתָא דְנַעָמִיתָא, וְלִיקְלֵי,
phrases.english: And if not, bring an ostrich egg and burn it,
and place it in linen rags in the summer
and in cotton rags in the winter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next two cures if step 6 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fine flour on the lower body, or ostrich egg ashes in rags, are cures for a זבה.

steps.title: A wine barrel, and the barley grain that ends the list
steps.stepSummary: Open a barrel of wine in her name. If that fails, she holds a barley grain found in a white donkey's dung. The longer she holds it, the longer the flow stops, and after three days it stops forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, open a barrel of wine for her. And if not, let her hold a barley grain found in the dung of a white donkey. If she holds it one day, the flow stops for two days. If she holds it two days, it stops for three days. If she holds it three days, it stops forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last cures on the זבה list. The final cure ends with a permanent result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The barley-grain cure is built on a growing scale: 1 day of holding gives 2 days of relief, 2 gives 3, and 3 gives permanent relief. This is the close of the זבה section before the גמרא moves on to ירקון.
steps.whatToRemember: The cures for a זבה form one long chain linked by וְאִי לָא. The chain moves from drinks, to frights, to things spread on the body, to ashes in rags, and ends with the barley grain that stops the flow forever.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לִיפְתַּח לַהּ חָבִיתָא דְחַמְרָא לִשְׁמַהּ.
phrases.english: And if not, open for her a barrel of wine in her name.
And if not, let her hold a barley grain
that is found in the dung of a white donkey,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָקְטָה חַד יוֹמָא — פָּסְקָה תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי,
phrases.english: if she holds it one day, it stops for two days,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי נָקְטָה תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי — פָּסְקָה תְּלָתָא יוֹמֵי,
phrases.english: and if she holds it two days, it stops for three days,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי נָקְטָה תְּלָתָא יוֹמֵי — פָּסְקָה לְעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: and if she holds it three days, it stops forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא — לִיפְתַּח לַהּ חָבִיתָא דְחַמְרָא לִשְׁמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final cures on the זבה list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A barley grain from a white donkey's dung, held for three days, stops the flow permanently.

steps.title: Turning to jaundice: two ingredients in beer, then a salted fish head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to ירקון. Two of the ingredients of the כוס של עיקרין (which the גמרא listed on the previous amud), drunk in beer, cure it but cause sterility. If that does not work, boil the head of a salted שיבוטא fish in beer and drink it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For jaundice: two (of the ingredients) in beer, and he becomes sterile. And if not, bring the head of a salted שיבוטא fish, boil it in beer, and drink it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: cures for ירקון, the illness named in the משנה. It explains the משנה's drink and then starts a new 'if not' chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed a כוס של עיקרין for ירקון. Here we learn that taking two of its ingredients in beer cures the illness but causes sterility (וּמִיעֲקַר). The next cure is for someone who cannot or will not use that drink.
steps.whyThisMatters: The sterility side effect is what leads the גמרא, later on this amud, to ask whether this drink is allowed at all, given the איסור of סירוס.

phrases.english: For jaundice, two in beer, and he becomes sterile.
phrases.notes: 'Two' refers to two of the three ingredients of the כוס של עיקרין.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לַיְיתֵי רֵישָׁא דְשִׁיבּוּטָא דְּמִילְחָא
phrases.english: And if not, bring the head of a salted shibuta fish
and boil it in beer, and drink it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the זבה list to the ירקון of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two ingredients in beer cure ירקון but cause sterility; a salted fish head in beer is an alternative.

steps.title: Brine, the bathhouse, and sweating by the oven
steps.stepSummary: Next comes grasshopper brine, or the brine of small birds if there is none. He smears it on himself in a bathhouse, and if there is no bathhouse, he stands between the oven and the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, bring grasshopper brine. If there is no grasshopper brine, bring the brine of small birds. Bring him into a bathhouse and smear him with it. If there is no bathhouse, stand him between the oven and the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps adding backup options. It even gives backups for when an ingredient or a place is not available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new phrase appears here: וְאִי לֵיכָּא ('and if there isn't'). Until now, 'if not' meant the cure failed. Here it means something is missing. The heat of the bathhouse or the oven is meant to make him sweat out the illness.

phrases.english: And if not, bring grasshopper brine.
And if there is no grasshopper brine,
bring brine of small birds,
and bring him into the bathhouse and smear him.
And if there is no bathhouse,
stand him between the oven and the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next ירקון cure, with backup options built in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brine smeared on the body in a hot place is a cure for ירקון.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: wrap him in his sheet to warm him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that anyone who wants to warm the patient should wrap him tightly in his sheet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whoever wants to warm him should wrap him in his sheet.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a practical tip to the heat cure from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cure in step 10 works by making the patient sweat. רבי יוחנן gives a simple way to hold in the heat: wrap the patient in his sheet.

keyTerms.meaning: He should wrap him (literally, wipe him)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who wants to warm him should wrap him in his sheet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the heat cure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wrapping the patient in his sheet helps warm him.

steps.title: רב כהנא heals רב אחא בר יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יוסף had ירקון. רב כהנא used this cure on him, and he was healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יוסף suffered from it. רב כהנא did this for him, and he was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing that the cure worked in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is being challenged here. The story backs up the cure with a real case. It shows that the remedy was actually used by חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יוֹסֵף חַשׁ בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yosef suffered from it,
Rav Kahana did it for him, and he was healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יוֹסֵף חַשׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the cure with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: That the heat-and-brine cure for ירקון works
steps.raayaSupportSource: The healing of רב אחא בר יוסף by רב כהנא

steps.title: Dates, wax and aloe boiled in beer
steps.stepSummary: The next ירקון cure is three containers each of Persian dates, dripping wax and red aloe, boiled in beer and drunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, bring three containers of Persian dates, three containers of dripping wax, and three containers of red aloe. Boil them in beer and drink it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its ירקון list after the story and gives the next drink cure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every ingredient here comes in a set of three containers. Like the earlier ירקון cures, it is cooked in beer (שִׁיכְרָא), not wine as in the זבה list.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי תְּלָתָא קְפִיזִי תַּמְרֵי פָּרְסְיָיתָא,
phrases.english: And if not, bring three containers of Persian dates,
and three containers of dripping wax,
and three containers of red aloe,
and boil them in beer, and drink it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי תְּלָתָא קְפִיזִי תַּמְרֵי פָּרְסְיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ירקון list after the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dates, wax and aloe boiled in beer are a cure for ירקון.

steps.title: Blood from a donkey foal placed on the head
steps.stepSummary: Shave the middle of a donkey foal's head, let blood from its forehead, and put it on the patient's head, taking care that it does not get into his eyes and blind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, bring a donkey foal and shave the middle of its head. Let blood from its forehead and place it on his head. He must be careful with his eyes, so that it does not blind them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an unusual cure that comes with a safety warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning (וְלִיזְדְּהַר) shows that the גמרא knew some cures had dangers. The blood must be kept away from the eyes, or it could cause blindness.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי עִילָא בַּר חֲמָרָא,
phrases.english: And if not, bring a donkey foal,
and shave the middle of its head,
and let blood from its forehead,
and place it on his own head,
and let him beware for his eyes, lest it blind them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי עִילָא בַּר חֲמָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next cure if step 13 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Donkey-foal blood on the head is a cure for ירקון, with care to protect the eyes.

steps.title: Pickled ram's head, a striped pig, and sharp leeks
steps.stepSummary: The last ירקון cures here: a pickled ram's head boiled in beer, a striped 'other thing' (a pig) torn open and placed on the heart, and leeks from the middle of the row.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, bring a pickled ram's head, boil it in beer, and drink it. And if not, bring a striped 'other thing' (a pig), tear it open, and place it on his heart. And if not, bring leeks from the middle of the row.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three more ירקון cures in a row, one after another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דָּבָר אַחֵר ('something else') is the polite way the גמרא names a pig, to avoid saying the word directly. The leeks from the middle of the row are the sharpest ones.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Something else' (a polite name for a pig)

steps.confusionAlert: דָּבָר אַחֵר here does not mean 'another explanation,' its common meaning in מדרש. Here it is a polite way of saying 'pig.'
steps.whatToRemember: The ירקון list works just like the זבה list. It is one chain of backup cures linked by וְאִי לָא, with רבי יוחנן's tip and the story of רב כהנא healing רב אחא בר יוסף along the way.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי רֵישָׁא דְּבַרְחָא דְּמַנַּח בְּכִיבְשָׁא,
phrases.english: And if not, bring a ram's head that was put in pickling,
and boil it in beer, and drink it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר חוּטְרָנָא,
phrases.english: And if not, bring a striped 'other thing' (pig),
and tear it open, and place it on his heart.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי כַּרָּתֵי מִכַּבְתְּוָתָא דְּמֵישָׁרֵי.
phrases.english: And if not, bring leeks from the middle of the row.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא — לַיְתֵי רֵישָׁא דְּבַרְחָא דְּמַנַּח בְּכִיבְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next three cures if step 14 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pickled ram's head, a striped pig on the heart, or sharp leeks are further cures for ירקון.

steps.title: The Arab who cured his jaundice with leeks and a borrowed cloak
steps.stepSummary: A sick Arab traded his cloak for a row of leeks and ate it. He then borrowed the gardener's cloak and slept wrapped in it. He sweated so much that the cloak fell apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain Arab had ירקון. He told a gardener: 'Take my cloak and give me a row of leeks.' The gardener gave it, and he ate it. Then he said: 'Lend me your cloak so I can sleep in it a little.' He wrapped himself in it and slept. When he got hot and stood up, the cloak fell off him in little pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing the leek cure and the 'wrap him up to warm him' advice actually working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cures from the earlier steps appear together here. Eating leeks (step 15) and being wrapped tightly to heat up (step 11) brought out such a strong sweat that the cloak fell apart. Some explain that the side detail is that the Arab tricked the gardener, who in the end got nothing out of the deal.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a halachic story. It is a medical anecdote. The cloak falling apart shows how much the sick man sweated out the illness.

phrases.english: A certain Arab who was sick with it (jaundice)
said to the gardener:
Take my cloak
and give me a row of leeks.
He gave it to him, and he ate it.
He said to him: Lend me your cloak
and I will sleep in it a little.
He wrapped himself and slept in it.
When he got hot and stood up,
it fell off him bit by bit.
phrases.notes: The cloak disintegrated from the heat and sweat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the leek cure from step 15 together with the warming advice from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The effectiveness of leeks plus heavy warming as a ירקון cure
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about a טייעא who cured himself this way

steps.title: Returning to the jaundice drink that causes sterility
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again an earlier line: for ירקון, drink two of the ingredients in beer, and the man becomes sterile.
steps.simpleTranslation: For ירקון: two (of the ingredients) in beer, and he becomes sterile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes a line it said earlier about a ירקון drink. This sets up the question that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא listed the ingredients of the 'כוס של עיקרין' (sterility drink). It said that for ירקון one drinks two of them in beer, and as a side effect the man becomes sterile. The גמרא repeats this line now because it is about to ask whether this is permitted.

phrases.english: For jaundice: two (ingredients) in beer,
and he becomes sterile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the anecdote and returns to an earlier recipe, so the גמרא can question it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ירקון drink of two ingredients in beer cures, but makes the man sterile.

steps.title: Is it allowed? Castrating a person is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this drink can be allowed, since a ברייתא of רבי חנינא learns from a פסוק that סירוס of a person is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is this permitted? But a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that castrating a person is forbidden? The פסוק says 'and in your land you shall not do,' meaning 'to yourselves you shall not do.' These are the words of רבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ירקון drink. Making a man sterile seems to break the איסור of סירוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא, which is about animals with damaged reproductive organs, ends with 'ובארצכם לא תעשו.' רבי חנינא reads 'בארצכם' as 'בכם,' meaning among yourselves, so people may not be castrated either. A drink that makes a man sterile seems to fall under this איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it permitted? (opening a challenge)
But it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the איסור of סירוס in people, which matters for halachic questions about medical treatments that cause sterility.

phrases.english: And is it permitted?
But it was taught (in a ברייתא):
From where do we know that castration of a person is forbidden?
The verse teaches: 'And in your land you shall not do'
meaning: to yourselves you shall not do it,
these are the words of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the recipe just quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission to drink a ירקון cure that causes sterility
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sterilizing a person is a form of סירוס, which רבי חנינא forbids based on 'ובארצכם לא תעשו.'

steps.title: The prohibition applies only when one intends to sterilize
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the איסור applies only when one acts in order to castrate. Here the sterility comes on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only where he intends it. Here, it happens by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer: the איסור of סירוס covers only someone who sets out to castrate. Here, the person is drinking a cure, and the sterility just happens by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer draws a line between direct, intended castration and sterility that comes indirectly. The drink is taken to heal ירקון, and the sterility is only a side effect, so it may fall outside the איסור.

phrases.english: These words (the prohibition) apply
where he intends (to castrate);
here, it happens on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the איסור (direct and intended acts versus indirect results)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any act that leads to sterility is forbidden סירוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only intentional, direct castration is forbidden. Sterility that comes on its own is not.

steps.title: Proof from the rooster whose comb is removed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs the answer with רבי יוחנן: to castrate a rooster, remove its comb and it becomes castrated on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: One who wants to castrate a rooster should remove its comb, and it becomes castrated by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for the idea that indirect sterilizing is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן gives this method as acceptable advice. That suggests that causing sterility indirectly, 'מאליו,' does not count as forbidden סירוס. This fits the answer in step 19.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who wants to castrate a rooster
should remove its comb,
and it becomes castrated on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיְּסָרֵס תַּרְנְגוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 19.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's advice about removing a rooster's comb

steps.title: רב אשי: the rooster is not truly castrated
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that removing the comb only takes away the rooster's pride. It stops mating but is not actually castrated, so the proof fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב אשי said: It is pride that holds it. (Removing the comb just humbles it. It is not real castration.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the rooster proof from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אשי, the rooster's comb gives it confidence. Once the comb is gone, the rooster is depressed and stops mating, but its body is not sterilized. Since no real סירוס happens there, the case proves nothing about indirect castration.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ashi say:
It is arrogance that takes hold of it.
phrases.notes: Without the comb, it loses its pride and stops mating. It is not actually castrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: רָמוּת רוּחָא הוּא דִּנְקִיטָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the ראיה of step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The rooster proof only. The rooster is not actually castrated.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Removing the comb affects behavior, not the body, so it is not a case of indirect סירוס.

steps.title: Rather, the drink is for someone already a castrate
steps.stepSummary: With the first answer weakened, the גמרא gives a new answer: the ירקון drink is meant for a סריס, who cannot be made sterile anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to a סריס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first approach and gives a new answer. The drink is permitted only for a man who is already a סריס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the rooster proof falls, the 'it happens by itself' answer loses its support. So the גמרא solves the problem differently: if the patient is already a סריס, the drink causes no new sterility, and there is no איסור at all.
steps.whatToRemember: After the rooster proof falls, the גמרא limits the sterility-causing ירקון drink to a סריס, someone who is already sterile. Step 23 immediately begins challenging this answer too, so it is not yet the final word.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'אלא' signals that the earlier answer ('מעצמו הוא') has been set aside. Do not combine the two answers.

phrases.english: Rather, (it is speaking) about a castrate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the תירוץ of step 19 after step 21 removed its support.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The drink is allowed because indirect sterility is not forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drink is allowed only for someone already a סריס, so no new סירוס takes place.

steps.title: A new challenge opens, quoting רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge to the 'סריס' answer by quoting רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן. The content continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חייא בר אבא say in the name of רבי יוחנן:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to challenge the answer it just gave, and the actual quote comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'והאמר' tells us an objection is coming. Here we only see who is being quoted. The point of the challenge, which will question whether even a סריס may be further sterilized, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often reports the teachings of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: The quoted statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the 'בסריס' answer of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the drink is permitted for a סריס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated. The quote from רבי יוחנן follows on the next amud.
